summary: Georgia's Government Resolution No. 255 (last amended on 24 February 2026) lists the countries whose citizens can enter Georgia visa-free and stay for a full year, among them the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, Turkey, Russia and Ukraine; Chinese citizens may stay 30 days, for tourism only. Resolution No. 256 lets holders of a visa or residence permit from a listed country, such as the US, the UK or Germany, enter visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period. Others apply for an ordinary visa, which can be obtained through the e-Visa portal.

name.text: A Georgian visa shall be divided into the following categories: Diplomatic (A) Special (B) Ordinary (C) Immigration (D) Transit (T) There are short-term and long-term visas with the right of a single entry or multiple entries.

method.text: Obtain Georgian visa of any type through the Georgian Embassy or Consular Office.

processing.text: The decision to issue a visa is made within the following time limits after a visa application is submitted: Short-term visa – 10 calendar days

passportValidity.text: Georgia's e-Visa portal says the travel document must be valid for at least 3 months after the validity period of the requested Georgian visa, have at least 2 free pages, not be damaged and have been issued within the previous 10 years. No official source we could read states a separate rule for visa-free visitors.

source.name: Georgia e-VISA Portal (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) — FAQ: document requirements and crossing the border

travelInsurance.text: Since 1 January 2026 all tourists entering Georgia must hold health and accident insurance covering the whole stay, including the arrival and departure dates, with a sum insured of at least GEL 30,000, issued by a Georgian or foreign insurer and shown on paper or electronically in Georgian or English. Exempt are holders of diplomatic and special visas; holders of diplomatic, official, service and special passports; accredited staff of diplomatic missions, consulates and international organisations and their accredited family members; persons whose entry is provided for by Georgia's international treaties; and drivers in international road freight and passenger transport.

source.name: Geoconsul (MFA of Georgia) — Entering Georgia
source.instrument: Law of Georgia on Tourism — mandatory health and accident insurance for tourists from 1 January 2026

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states a return or onward ticket requirement. Georgia's e-Visa portal lists the documents visa holders must carry at the border (passport, proof of the purpose of travel, accommodation, insurance and funds) without a ticket.

source.name: Georgia e-VISA Portal (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) — FAQ: document requirements and crossing the border

proofOfFunds.text: Georgia's e-Visa portal says visa holders crossing the border should carry a document proving sufficient financial means, such as a bank statement for the past three months, a reference from the employer stating position and income, a document proving ownership of real estate, or a letter from a sponsor. No official source we could read states an amount, or a funds requirement for visa-free visitors.

source.name: Georgia e-VISA Portal (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) — FAQ: document requirements and crossing the border

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Georgia?
faq.answer: No. The United States is on the list in Georgia's Government Resolution No. 255, whose citizens can enter Georgia visa-free and stay for a full year.

faq.question: How long can I really stay in Georgia visa-free?
faq.answer: A full year for citizens of the countries on Georgia's visa-free list (Government Resolution No. 255), among them the US, the UK, Germany, Canada, Australia, Japan, Turkey, Russia and Ukraine. Chinese citizens, also on the list, may stay 30 days, for tourism only.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Georgia, and how much is it?
faq.answer: Georgia's Consular Department says Indian citizens must obtain an ordinary visa for short-term visits, and that it can be obtained by applying through the e-Visa Portal. Under Government Resolution No. 256, holders of a visa or residence permit from a listed country, such as the US, the UK, Germany or the UAE, can instead enter visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period. The e-Visa portal gives the fee as USD 20 plus a 2% service fee, and says the e-Visa's validity varies according to the country of the passport.

faq.question: Can I enter Georgia with a Schengen, US or UK visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Under Georgia's Government Resolution No. 256, holders of a visa or residence permit from a listed country, among them the US, the UK, Germany, the UAE and other Gulf states, can enter Georgia without a visa and stay for 90 calendar days in any 180-day period; the visa or permit must be valid on the day of entry.

faq.question: Can I visit Abkhazia or South Ossetia from Georgia?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to the Russian-occupied regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia and all but essential travel to areas immediately next to their administrative boundary lines, and says it cannot provide face-to-face support to British nationals there.

entryRequirements.travelInsurance.text: In accordance with the Law of Georgia "On Tourism", starting from January 01, 2026 , all tourists entering Georgia are required to hold a valid health and accident insurance policy. Any tourist entering the territory of Georgia must present a valid health and accident insurance policy in either physical or electronic form and must be available in Georgian or English. The insurance policy may be issued by either a Georgian or a foreign insurance company, and the insurance coverage amount must be no less than 30 000 GEL.

The insurance policy is required to cover the full period of a tourist’s stay in Georgia, including both arrival and departure dates. The following persons are exempt from mandatory requirement of insurance: • Holders of diplomatic and special visas; • Holders of diplomatic, official, service and special passports; • Accredited employees of diplomatic missions, consular representations, representation offices of international organizations and equivalent representation offices, as well as their family members who hold an accreditation; • Persons whose entering to Georgia is envisaged by International Treaties and Agreements of Georgia; • Drivers engaged in international road freight and passenger transportation.
